records.value: Learners complete an independent multi-step summative assessment task set on the shores of Lake Victoria near Kisumu. The problem reads: 'A lighthouse stands at the edge of a cliff on the shore of Lake Victoria. A fisherman in a boat is 120 m (horizontal distance) from the foot of the cliff. From the boat he sees the top of the cliff at an angle of elevation of 22° and the top of the lighthouse at an angle of elevation of 38°. Treat the fisherman's eye level as the water level. (a) Draw a labelled diagram. (b) Calculate the height of the cliff above the water and the height of the top of the lighthouse above the water, each to 1 decimal place. (c) Hence find the height of the lighthouse itself. (d) A coastguard at the top of the lighthouse looks down at the boat. What is the angle of depression? Give a reason without calculating. (e) Challenge: the coastguard sees a second boat, in line with the first and further from the cliff, at an angle of depression of 20°. How far is the second boat from the foot of the cliff, and how far from the first boat (to the nearest metre)?' Learners work independently in silence for 18 minutes (part (e) is a challenge for learners who finish early). After submitting, they swap with a partner and peer-mark using a teacher-written mark scheme displayed on the board, then write one sentence in their notebooks reflecting on which of the two Kenyan professionals, the fisherman navigating Lake Victoria or the coastguard, is making the more safety-critical calculation and why.
records.why: The old task was geometrically impossible: the fisherman's angle of elevation to the lighthouse top (38°) and the coastguard's angle of depression to the same boat (22°) lie along the same line of sight and must be equal. The mark scheme itself ran into contradictions (negative cliff height) and ended with 'an inconsistency designed to promote critical thinking', which is not acceptable in a summative task. The new task keeps the 120 m, 22° and 38° values and the Lake Victoria setting but uses two different lines of sight from the boat (to the cliff top and to the lighthouse top), so the heights are positive and consistent (cliff 48.5 m, lighthouse top 93.8 m, lighthouse 45.3 m). Part (d) uses the elevation = depression rule from Lesson 7 and part (e) uses depression in a calculation. All values were recomputed: 120 × tan 22° = 48.48 m, 120 × tan 38° = 93.75 m, difference 45.27 m, depression back to the boat = 38°, second boat 93.75 ÷ tan 20° = 257.6 m from the cliff and 137.6 m beyond the first boat. Teachers should confirm they like the context.
records.reference: OpenStax, Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, Chapter 7 (right-triangle applications: angles of elevation and depression, measured from the horizontal); KICD Grade 10 Core Mathematics curriculum design, Sub-Strand 2.4

A coastguard at the top of the lighthouse observes the same boat at an angle of depression of 22°. (a) Calculate the height of the lighthouse above the water. (b) Calculate the height of the cliff (to the nearest metre). (c) Hence find the total height of the lighthouse structure above the base of the cliff.' Show all working. You have 18 minutes. Begin.' Set a visible timer for 18 minutes. Circulate continuously. Check your diagram.' At the 10-minute mark, give a time warning: 'Eight minutes remaining. If you have not yet started part (c), move to it now.' At 18 minutes, say 'Pens down. Swap books with your partner.' Display the mark scheme and read each step aloud. (b) Cliff: tan 22° = h₁ ÷ 120, so h₁ = 120 × tan 22° ≈ 120 × 0.4040 ≈ 48.5 m. Top of lighthouse: tan 38° = h₂ ÷ 120, so h₂ = 120 × tan 38° ≈ 120 × 0.7813 ≈ 93.8 m. (c) Lighthouse height = h₂ − h₁ ≈ 93.8 − 48.5 = 45.3 m. (d) The angle of depression is 38°. The coastguard's line of sight to the boat is the same line as the fisherman's line of sight to the lighthouse top, and the horizontal at the lighthouse top is parallel to the water, so the two angles are alternate angles and are equal. Check: tan⁻¹(93.8 ÷ 120) ≈ 38°. (e) tan 20° = 93.8 ÷ d, so d = 93.8 ÷ 0.3640 ≈ 258 m from the foot of the cliff, which is about 138 m beyond the first boat (258 − 120). records.value: Teacher collects peer-marked scripts at the end of the phase. Use the CBE levels. Exceeds Expectations: a correct diagram showing both lines of sight; (b) to (d) all correct with units; explains in (d) that depression equals elevation because they are alternate angles; completes or nearly completes (e). Approaches Expectations: the diagram or ratio is mostly right but one stage is wrong, for example forgetting to subtract the cliff height in (c) or inverting the ratio; (d) answered without a reason. Below Expectations: no diagram, or opposite and adjacent are confused so that no stage is correct. Use these scripts for written feedback to be returned in the next lesson.

records.old: The side opposite the 40° angle is the mast height h, and this same side is adjacent to the 50° angle. The hypotenuse is the same for both angles. So sin 40° = opposite ÷ hypotenuse = h ÷ hypotenuse, and cos 50° = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse = h ÷ hypotenuse.
records.new: The side opposite the 40° angle (at the top of the mast) is the 40 m ground distance, and this same side is adjacent to the 50° angle. The hypotenuse is the same for both angles. So sin 40° = opposite ÷ hypotenuse = 40 ÷ hypotenuse, and cos 50° = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse = 40 ÷ hypotenuse.
records.why: The model answer said the mast height h is opposite the 40° angle. It is not: the 40° angle is at the top of the mast, so the side opposite it is the 40 m ground distance, and h is opposite the 50° angle. As written, the explanation would show sin 50° = cos 40° and not the requested sin 40° = cos 50°. Checked: sin 40° = cos 50° = 40 ÷ 62.2 = 0.6428.
